notes: Focused public C++ and Java TCK evidence for IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.12.4.2 p. 382 l. 24-7. The C++ scenario obtains valid handles for every Handle class declared in the pinned 2025 C++ API, verifies each Handle::encode result decodes and re-encodes byte-identically as HLAvariableArray<HLAbyte> using the official C++ HLAvariableArrayT<HLAoctet>, and uses the corresponding RTIambassador typed decoder for each handle kind where the public API defines one. The Java counterpart obtains the same ten handle kinds through standard RTI services, checks their encoded bytes through HLAvariableArray<HLAbyte>, and decodes them with the standard handle factories. Java exposes a TransportationTypeHandleFactory decoder in addition to the nine C++ RTIambassador decoders. Neither scenario asserts an implementation-specific handle byte layout or independent-provider conformance.
